Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Daniel, Priya, Arjun (StellarBridge)
Recorded: yes

Auto-summary (generated):
StellarBridge and Redwood reviewed week-3 POC lab results comparing Redwood runtime against their incumbent provider (IncumbentAI). Redwood showed better median latency at 512 tokens and comparable throughput per GPU with quantized models, but the customer observed sporadic tail-latency spikes during burst patterns. Action items assigned to share routing/quantization playbook, run an extended KV-cache enabled test, and schedule a low-latency deep dive.

Topics covered: latency delta vs baseline, throughput scaling, quantization profiles (4/8-bit tradeoffs), KV cache prefix hits, fallback policies, dedicated slot requests, security/observability notes.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep this tight — agenda is quick readout on the lab numbers and then triage the tail-latency spikes Priya flagged.
00:12 Daniel (StellarBridge): Yep, thanks Maya. We had the team run the head-to-head overnight, we combined our standard customer prompt-set with 20% longer completions to stress KV cache behavior.
00:22 Priya (ML Infra): Quick note — we used the same input set against IncumbentAI and Redwood Dedicated instance that Liam provisioned. we saw median latency improvement but some outliers.
00:34 Liam (SE): Cool, so the headline: median 512-token latency down ~18% vs IncumbentAI on the same GPU class, throughput across the cluster was within 5%, unit-cost slightly lower on Redwood with our batching + prefix cache.
00:50 Arjun (CTO): When you say unit-cost lower, what's included? does that factor in reserved vs on-demand?
00:57 Maya: Good question. This is purely per-token runtime cost from the lab run — doesn't bake in committed reserved pricing. we'll send a cost projection for reserved/dedicated later.
01:07 Priya: The concerning part was spikes — p99 and p999 are worse at certain traffic patterns. sometimes we see a jump around 400-700ms for requests that were previously 150-200ms.
01:21 Liam: Right — we investigated traces. two likely causes: cold KV cache misses on longer prefixes, and occasional quantization kernel fallback for certain ops when sequence length grows. also one of the routing rules routed to a smaller instance when autoscaling misfired under a burst test.
01:40 Daniel: That routing misfire is interesting — we forced a burst with 400 concurrent short requests to emulate peak. Redwood fell back to a lower-tier pool?
01:49 Maya: There was an autoscale policy misalignment — the test run used a default burst config, not the reserved burst. we have a suggested policy in the playbook to prefer warm slots for tail-sensitive traffic. we'll share that.
02:00 Priya: Could you explain the quantization fallback? we thought 4-bit would be deterministic.
02:06 Liam: In most paths it is, but for some attention kernel patterns with very long key sequences, our runtime chooses a different kernel to preserve numerical stability — that can temporarily add a small overhead. we tracked which model layers trigger it.
02:20 Arjun: Is that something we can tune — like limit max prefix length or change KV eviction?
02:26 Liam: Yes, options: cap KV cache TTL, use partial prefix caching for long-running sessions, or pick a quantization profile that avoids that kernel. tradeoff is slight quality delta — we'll show the evals.
02:38 Priya: We need to see exact prompts that hit the worst p999. I'll share sample request IDs post-call.
02:44 Daniel: Also, IncumbentAI had more stable tail latency but at higher median — wonder if they were doing more conservative batching or less aggressive kernel selection.
02:55 Maya: Right, tradeoff is conservative kernel selection vs median speed. Our thesis is to provide knobs for latency-sensitive apps. for pilot purposes we can tune to match their tail at the cost of median and show both.
03:08 Priya: One more thing — logging. we want token-level tracing and the ability to correlate token emission with kvcache hit/miss. can Redwood provide that in the lab mode?
03:18 Liam: Yes, we can enable debug traces for specific request IDs; it will include KV hit flags and kernel switching. there is a small perf impact while traces are enabled, so we'll do it on a sample set.
03:30 Daniel: Good. Also, what about the fallback policy? we noticed a fallback to Redwood-hosted smaller variants, can we force fallback to model variant with conservatively tuned quantization instead?
03:41 Maya: Absolutely — routing policy can prefer a "stable-variant" under load. we have a playbook with routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and stable-first. we'll attach it.
03:52 Priya: We attempted a run enabling KV-cache and saw 12% throughput improvement but weird spike behavior remained during multi-tenant bursts.
04:03 Liam: Multi-tenancy can cause noisy neighbors if autoscale thresholds are too sticky. proposed tweak: shorten scaling cooldown and reserve a small dedicated headroom for their tenant during business hours.
04:17 Arjun: How much headroom are we talking about to remove spikes?
04:21 Liam: In these tests, reserving ~10% of capacity as warm reserved slots dropped p999 by ~30% in the lab. Will send the exact numbers.
04:31 Priya: Sounds promising. We need to confirm cost delta for that headroom.
04:35 Maya: We'll produce a cost delta sheet — rough estimate in the playbook now, detailed numbers in the spreadsheet.
04:43 Daniel: Security note — our audit team asked if debug traces and token-level logs can be redacted automatically and if logs can be sent to our S3 with SSE-KMS.
04:54 Liam: Yes, Redwood supports pushing audit logs to customer S3 and integrating KMS. we'll include steps to enable redaction filters for PII.
05:05 Priya: Any differences in model quality after 4-bit quant? incurrent provider maintained quality apparently.
05:12 Liam: We ran the eval harness, overall rouge/bleu-ish metrics had <1% delta for our chosen profiles. some corner cases — named entities and long-number sequences — showed small regressions. we'll share the eval set.
05:27 Arjun: Ok next steps then?
05:30 Maya: Action items: Liam will prepare microbench script for tail tests; Priya will run KV-enabled set and post logs; Maya will send playbook + annotated spreadsheet. we'll reconvene mid-next-week for the deep dive.
05:41 Daniel: One more ask — can we get a short run with dedicated slots reserved for 48 hours so we can reproduce spikes in isolation?
05:48 Maya: Yes we can spin up a dedicated reservation for 48 hours for the test. we'll need confirmation of window and preferred instance types.
05:56 Priya: We'll confirm offline, thanks.
06:00 Maya: Great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and folder.
